one_sentence_story: Kahneman and Tversky proved in 1979 that humans judge choices from a shifting reference point where losing stings roughly twice as hard as winning feels good — turning cautious savers in gains into desperate gamblers trying to dodge a sure loss.
so_what_for_you: Before doubling down on a losing project or subscription just to 'get back to even,' reset your reference point to zero and ask: 'If I were starting fresh today, would I choose this?'

jargon_map.plain: psychological asymmetry where losing a given amount hurts roughly twice as intensely as gaining that exact same amount delights
jargon_map.analogy: like dropping an ice cream cone hurting twice as much as finding a free scoop

jargon_map.plain: the mental zero-line (current status quo or expectation) against which gains and losses are felt
jargon_map.analogy: like step-out room temperature making 65°F pool water feel freezing after a sauna or warm after snow

jargon_map.plain: flipping from cautious risk-avoidance on gains to risky gambling when trying to dodge a sure loss
